To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DSM can be modeled and simulated on the distribution system level, that the distribution system is the best level to evaluate DSM impact, and that the distribution system level is also a good level for evaluating DSM impact on reliability.

1) The impact of DSM on distribution systems depends on the type of DSM and on the distribution system characteristics; 2) DSM has the greatest impact on distribution systems with low load factors and high peak-to-average power ratios; 3) DSM can be beneficial for distribution systems with low peak-to-average power ratio and low load factor, but not beneficial for high peak-to-average ratio and high load factor systems; 4) DSM can be detrimental for distribution systems with medium to high load factors

DSM programs can be analyzed using computer techniques developed for distribution plan analysis and that a fast screening model can provide a good estimate of the impact of DSM on distribution systems.

the development and evaluation of techniques to assist utilities in the planning of DSM programs, particularly in regard to the impact of DSM on distribution system planning and operation.
developing techniques to evaluate the impact of DSM on the distribution system and to provide a basis for determining whether a given DSM technique will be beneficial to a distribution company.
the development of techniques for the design, operation, and planning of distribution systems with the inclusion of DSM.
